sub_questions.text: (क) अतुल, बीना तथा सीता एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 8:7:5 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे। दामिनी को लाभों में 1/5 भाग के लिए एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया गया, जो उसने पूर्ण रूप से अतुल से अधिग्रहित किया । दामिनी के प्रवेश के बाद नया लाभ-विभाजन अनुपात होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Atul, Beena and Sita were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 8:7:5. Damini was admitted as a new partner for 1/5th share in the profits which she acquired entirely from Atul. The new profit sharing ratio after Damini's admission will be:
sub_questions.solution: Damini acquires her entire 1/5th share (which is equivalent to 4/20) from Atul. Atul's original share was 8/20, so his new share becomes 8/20 - 4/20 = 4/20. Beena and Sita retain their original shares of 7/20 and 5/20 respectively, making the new profit sharing ratio 4:7:5:4.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) Rushil and Abheer were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4: 3. They admitted Sunil as a new partner for 3/7th share in the profits of firm, which he acquired 2/7th share from Rushil and 1/7th share from Abheer. The new profit sharing ratio of Rushil, Abheer and Sunil will be :
sub_questions.solution: Sunil receives 2/7 from Rushil and 1/7 from Abheer. Rushil's new share is 4/7 - 2/7 = 2/7. Abheer's new share is 3/7 - 1/7 = 2/7. Therefore, the new profit sharing ratio among Rushil, Abheer, and Sunil is 2:2:3.

questions.text: अभय, बोरिस तथा चेतन एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 5:3:2 के अनुपात में लाभों का विभाजन करते थे । बोरिस को लाभ में ₹ 95,000 की गारंटी दी गई। इसके कारण हुई किसी भी कमी को अभय तथा चेतन बराबर-बराबर वहन करेंगे। 31 मार्च, 2023 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष में, फर्म ने ₹ 2,00,000 का लाभ अर्जित किया। अभय द्वारा बोरिस को उसकी गारंटी की राशि के रूप में दी गई राशि होगी :
questions.text_english: Abhay, Boris and Chetan were partners in a firm sharing profits in the ratio of 5:3: 2. Boris was guaranteed a profit of ₹ 95,000. Any deficiency on account of this was to be borne by Abhay and Chetan equally. The firm earned a profit of ₹ 2,00,000 for the year ended 31st March, 2023. The amount given by Abhay to Boris as guaranteed amount will be :
questions.solution: Boris's share of the actual profit is 3/10 of ₹2,00,000, which equals ₹60,000. His guaranteed minimum profit is ₹95,000, creating a deficiency of ₹35,000. This deficiency is borne equally by Abhay and Chetan, meaning Abhay must contribute half of it, which amounts to ₹17,500.
questions.solution_hindi: बोरिस का वास्तविक लाभ में हिस्सा ₹2,00,000 का 3/10, यानी ₹60,000 है। उसकी गारंटी की राशि ₹95,000 है, जिससे ₹35,000 की कमी उत्पन्न होती है। यह कमी अभय और चेतन द्वारा समान रूप से वहन की जानी है, इसलिए अभय द्वारा दी जाने वाली राशि ₹17,500 होगी।

questions.text: आव्या, मितांश तथा प्रवीन एक फर्म में साझेदार थे । 31 मार्च, 2023 को फर्म का विघटन हो गया । लेनदारों ने ₹50,000 पुस्तक मूल्य के फर्नीचर को उनके ₹ 60,000 की राशि के आंशिक निपटारे के रूप में ₹ 45,000 में ले लिया। शेष राशि का भुगतान उन्हें चैक द्वारा किया गया । चैक द्वारा भुगतान की जाने वाली राशि होगी :
questions.text_english: Aavya, Mitansh and Praveen were partners in a firm. On 31st March, 2023, the firm was dissolved. Creditors took over furniture of book value of ₹ 50,000 at ₹ 45,000 in part settlement of their amount of ₹ 60,000. The balance amount was paid to them through cheque. The amount paid through cheque will be :
questions.solution: The total amount owed to the creditors was ₹60,000. They accepted furniture valued at ₹45,000 for part settlement of their claim. The remaining balance to be paid by cheque is the difference between the total claim and the settlement value of the asset taken over, which is ₹60,000 minus ₹45,000, equalling ₹15,000.
questions.solution_hindi: लेनदारों की कुल देय राशि ₹60,000 थी। उन्होंने अपने दावों के आंशिक निपटारे के रूप में ₹45,000 मूल्य का फर्नीचर स्वीकार किया। शेष राशि जो चेक द्वारा भुगतान की जानी है, कुल देय राशि और ली गई संपत्ति के मूल्य का अंतर है, जो ₹60,000 - ₹45,000 = ₹15,000 है।

questions.text: पियूष, राजेश तथा अविनाश एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा लाभ-हानि का विभाजन बराबर-बराबर करते थे। शिवा को बराबर के भाग के लिए एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया गया । शिवा अपने भाग की पूँजी तथा ख्याति प्रीमियम नगद लाया । ख्याति प्रीमियम की राशि को विभाजित किया जाएगा :
questions.text_english: Piyush, Rajesh and Avinash were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses equally. Shiva was admitted as a new partner for an equal share. Shiva brought his share of capital and premium for goodwill in cash. The premium for goodwill amount will be divided among :

options.A: पुराने साझेदारों के बीच पुराने अनुपात में
options.B: नए साझेदारों के बीच नए अनुपात में
options.C: नए साझेदारों के बीच त्याग अनुपात में
options.D: पुराने साझेदारों के बीच त्याग अनुपात में

questions.solution: When a new partner brings in their share of the premium for goodwill in cash, this amount serves as compensation to the existing partners for the profit share they have relinquished. Therefore, it is always distributed among the old partners in their sacrificing ratio.
questions.solution_hindi: जब कोई नया साझेदार नकद में ख्याति के लिए प्रीमियम का अपना हिस्सा लाता है, तो यह राशि मौजूदा साझेदारों को उनके द्वारा छोड़े गए लाभ के हिस्से के लिए मुआवजे के रूप में कार्य करती है। इसलिए, इसे हमेशा पुराने साझेदारों के बीच उनके त्याग अनुपात में विभाजित किया जाता है।

questions.text: एलेक्स, बैन तथा कोल एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 5:3:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि विभाजित करते थे। उन्होंने डोना को भावी लाभों में 1/5 भाग के लिए एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया । डोना आनुपातिक पूँजी देने के लिए सहमत हो गई । प्रवेश की तिथि पर एलेक्स, बैन तथा कोल की पूँजी, सभी समायोजनों के पश्चात् क्रमशः ₹ 1,20,000, ₹ 80,000 तथा ₹ 1,00,000 थी। डोना द्वारा लाई गई पूँजी की राशि होगी :
questions.text_english: Alex, Benn and Cole were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3:2. They admitted Dona as a new partner for 1/5th share in the future profits. Dona agreed to contribute proportionate capital. On the date of admission, capitals of Alex, Benn and Cole after all adjustments were ₹ 1,20,000; ₹ 80,000 and ₹ 1,00,000 respectively. The amount of capital brought in by Dona will be:
questions.solution: The combined adjusted capital of the old partners (Alex, Benn, and Cole) is ₹1,20,000 + ₹80,000 + ₹1,00,000 = ₹3,00,000. Since Dona is admitted for a 1/5th share, the old partners retain a 4/5th share of the firm. Therefore, the total capital of the firm is calculated as ₹3,00,000 multiplied by the reciprocal of their share (5/4), which equals ₹3,75,000. Dona's proportionate capital contribution is 1/5th of the total firm capital, which is ₹75,000.
questions.solution_hindi: पुराने साझेदारों (एलेक्स, बैन और कोल) की कुल समायोजित पूंजी ₹1,20,000 + ₹80,000 + ₹1,00,000 = ₹3,00,000 है। चूंकि डोना को 1/5 भाग के लिए प्रवेश दिया गया है, इसलिए पुराने साझेदारों के पास फर्म का 4/5 भाग शेष रहता है। इसलिए, फर्म की कुल पूंजी ₹3,00,000 को उनके हिस्से के व्युत्क्रम (5/4) से गुणा करके निकाली जाती है, जो ₹3,75,000 है। डोना का आनुपातिक पूंजी योगदान कुल फर्म पूंजी का 1/5 वां हिस्सा है, जो ₹75,000 है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : प्रत्येक साझेदार प्रमुख होने के साथ-साथ दूसरे सभी साझेदारों के लिए एक अभिकर्ता भी है ।
कारण (R) : साझेदारी अधिनियम की परिभाषा के अनुसार, साझेदारी व्यवसाय सभी साझेदारों द्वारा या सभी की ओर से उनमें से किसी एक के द्वारा चलाया जा सकता है ।
निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Each partner is a principal as well as an agent for all the other partners.
Reason (R): As per the definition of Partnership Act, partnership business may be carried on by all the partners or any of them acting for all.
Choose the correct option from the following:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, लेकिन कारण (R) ग़लत है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, लेकिन कारण (R) सही है ।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is incorrect.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is incorrect, but Reason (R) is correct.

questions.solution: The mutual agency concept under the Partnership Act establishes that every partner operates as both an agent (binding others by their acts) and a principal (being bound by the acts of others). The Reason correctly defines this legal framework by stating that the business can be carried on by all or any of them acting for all, which directly explains the Assertion.
questions.solution_hindi: साझेदारी अधिनियम के तहत पारस्परिक एजेंसी की अवधारणा यह स्थापित करती है कि प्रत्येक साझेदार एक अभिकर्ता (अपने कार्यों द्वारा दूसरों को बाध्य करने वाला) और एक प्रमुख (दूसरों के कार्यों से बाध्य होने वाला) दोनों के रूप में कार्य करता है। कारण (R) सही ढंग से इस कानूनी ढांचे को परिभाषित करता है कि व्यवसाय सभी द्वारा या उन सभी की ओर से कार्य करने वाले किसी भी व्यक्ति द्वारा चलाया जा सकता है, जो सीधे अभिकथन (A) की व्याख्या करता है।

questions.text: आभा तथा बबीता मिट्टी से खिलौने बनाने वाली एक फर्म की साझेदार थीं तथा 2:1 के अनुपात में लाभों का विभाजन करती थीं । 1 अप्रैल, 2023 को उनके पूँजी खाते क्रमशः ₹ 5,00,000 तथा ₹ 10,00,000 के शेष दर्शा रहे थे। साझेदारी संलेख में 10% वार्षिक दर से पूँजी पर ब्याज देने का प्रावधान था। फर्म ने वर्ष के दौरान ₹90,000 का लाभ अर्जित किया । आभा को दिए जाने वाली पूँजी पर ब्याज की राशि होगी :
questions.text_english:
Read the following hypothetical situation and answer questions No. 7 and 8 on the basis of the given information.
Abha and Babita were partners in a clay toy making firm sharing profits in the ratio of 2: 1. On 1st April, 2023, their capital accounts showed balances of ₹5,00,000 and ₹10,00,000 respectively. The partnership deed provides for interest on capital @ 10% p.a. The firm earned a profit of ₹90,000 during the year.
The amount of interest on capital allowed to Abha will be:
questions.solution: The interest on capital calculated at 10% for Abha is ₹50,000 and for Babita is ₹1,00,000, bringing the total interest claim to ₹1,50,000. However, the firm's available profit is only ₹90,000. Because available profits are less than the total interest claim, the profit must be distributed in the ratio of their interest claims (50,000 : 1,00,000 = 1:2). Thus, Abha receives 1/3rd of ₹90,000, which is ₹30,000.
questions.solution_hindi: आभा के लिए 10% की दर से पूंजी पर ब्याज ₹50,000 और बबीता के लिए ₹1,00,000 है, जिससे कुल ब्याज का दावा ₹1,50,000 हो जाता है। हालांकि, फर्म का उपलब्ध लाभ केवल ₹90,000 है। क्योंकि उपलब्ध लाभ कुल ब्याज के दावे से कम है, इसलिए लाभ को उनके ब्याज के दावों के अनुपात (50,000 : 1,00,000 = 1:2) में वितरित किया जाना चाहिए। इस प्रकार, आभा को ₹90,000 का 1/3 हिस्सा मिलेगा, जो ₹30,000 है।
questions.topic: Interest on Capital when Profits are Inadequate

questions.text: बबीता का लाभ में भाग होगा :
questions.text_english: Babita's share in profit will be :
questions.solution: As the entire available profit of ₹90,000 was completely utilized to pay the proportionate interest on capital to both partners, no surplus profit is left over for distribution in their standard profit-sharing ratio. Consequently, Babita's residual share in the pure profit is Nil.
questions.solution_hindi: चूंकि ₹90,000 के संपूर्ण उपलब्ध लाभ का पूरी तरह से दोनों साझेदारों को पूंजी पर आनुपातिक ब्याज का भुगतान करने के लिए उपयोग किया गया था, इसलिए उनके मानक लाभ-साझाकरण अनुपात में वितरण के लिए कोई अतिरिक्त लाभ नहीं बचा है। परिणामस्वरूप, शुद्ध लाभ में बबीता का अवशिष्ट हिस्सा शून्य (कुछ नहीं) है।

questions.text: एल्फा लिमिटेड ने 30% प्रीमियम पर ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 50,000 समता अंशों/शेयरों के लिए आवेदन आमंत्रित किए । सम्पूर्ण राशि का भुगतान आवेदन पर किया जाना था । 2,50,000 अंशों/शेयरों के लिए आवेदन प्राप्त हुए । कम्पनी ने सभी आवेदकों को आनुपातिक आधार पर अंशों/शेयरों को आबंटित करने का निर्णय लिया । कम्पनी द्वारा वापिस की गई राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Alfa Ltd. invited applications for 50,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a premium of 30%. The whole amount was payable on application. Applications were received for 2,50,000 shares. The company decided to allot the shares on a pro-rata basis to all the applicants. The amount refunded by the company was:
questions.solution: The total issue price is ₹13 per share (₹10 face value plus ₹3 premium), and it was fully payable on application. The company received applications for 2,50,000 shares but can only allot a maximum of 50,000 shares. Since the entire amount was collected on application, all money received for the unallotted shares (2,50,000 - 50,000 = 2,00,000 shares) must be refunded directly. The refund amount is 2,00,000 shares multiplied by ₹13, which equals ₹26,00,000.

questions.text_english: Reserve capital is that part of ________ capital which cannot be called except at the time of winding up of the company.
questions.solution: Reserve capital represents the specific portion of a company's uncalled capital that the company has formally resolved not to call up except in the event of its winding up, essentially reserving it for the protection of its creditors.

ज़ीनो लिमिटेड ने ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 25,000 समता अंश/शेयर निर्गमित किए । राशि का भुगतान निम्न प्रकार से करना था :
आवेदन पर ₹4 प्रति अंश/शेयर
आबंटन पर ₹5 प्रति अंश/शेयर
प्रथम एवं अंतिम याचना पर शेष
प्रस्तावित सभी अंशों/शेयरों के लिए आवेदन प्राप्त हुए और आबंटित कर दिए गए । 1,500 अंशों/शेयरों को छोड़कर आबंटन पर देय समस्त धनराशि प्राप्त हो गईं। आबंटन के तुरंत बाद इन अंशों/शेयरों का हरण (forfeit) कर लिया गया । प्रथम एवं अंतिम याचना अभी तक माँगी नहीं गई थी। अंश/शेयर हरण (forfeit) के समय अंश/शेयर पूँजी खाते में नाम किए जाएँगे :
questions.text_english:
Xeno Ltd. issued 25,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each. The amount was payable as follows:
On Application ₹ 4 per share
On Allotment ₹ 5 per share
On First and Final call Balance
All the shares offered were applied for and allotted. All the money due on allotment was received except on 1,500 shares. These shares were forfeited immediately after allotment. First and final call was not yet made. At the time of forfeiture, Share Capital Account will be debited by:
questions.solution: When shares are forfeited, the Share Capital Account is debited with the called-up value of the shares up to the point of forfeiture. In this case, the called-up amount includes the application money (₹4) and the allotment money (₹5), making the called-up value ₹9 per share. For 1,500 forfeited shares, the Share Capital account will be debited by 1,500 multiplied by ₹9, which is ₹13,500.
questions.solution_hindi: जब अंशों का हरण किया जाता है, तो अंश पूंजी खाते को हरण के समय तक अंशों के मांगे गए (called-up) मूल्य से नाम (debit) किया जाता है। इस मामले में, मांगी गई राशि में आवेदन राशि (₹4) और आबंटन राशि (₹5) शामिल है, जिससे प्रति अंश मांगा गया मूल्य ₹9 हो जाता है। 1,500 हरण किए गए अंशों के लिए, अंश पूंजी खाते को 1,500 गुना ₹9 से नाम किया जाएगा, जो कि ₹13,500 है।

questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Irredeemable debentures are also known as perpetual debentures.
Reason (R): The company does not give any undertaking for the repayment of money borrowed by issuing such debentures. They are repayable on the winding up of the company or on the expiry of a long period.
Choose the correct option from the following:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, लेकिन कारण (R) सही है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) सही है, लेकिन कारण (R) ग़लत है ।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is incorrect, but Reason (R) is correct.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is incorrect.

questions.solution: Irredeemable debentures are indeed termed perpetual debentures precisely because the issuing company makes no commitment to repay the principal amount during its operational lifetime. Repayment only occurs upon the liquidation of the company, making the Reason a perfectly accurate explanation for the Assertion.

With effect from 1st April, 2023, they decided to change their profit sharing ratio to 2:3:5. There existed a General Reserve of ₹ 90,000 on the date of change in profit sharing ratio. The partners decided not to distribute General Reserve. The necessary adjustment entry to show the effect of the above will be:

options.B: Dan's Capital A/c Dr. 90,000; To Furhan's Capital A/c 90,000

The adjustment amount is ₹90,000 multiplied by the 3/10 gained/sacrificed, giving ₹27,000. Hence, Furhan's Capital is debited by ₹27,000 and Dan's is credited by ₹27,000.

Adding these gains to their original shares: Mita's new share is 3/6 + 1/30 = 16/30. Veena's new share is 2/6 + 4/30 = 14/30. The new ratio therefore becomes 16:14, which simplifies to 8:7.

questions.text:
आमीर, बशीर तथा चिराग एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 3:3:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । चिराग सेवानिवृत्त हो गया । आमीर तथा बशीर ने भविष्य में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन 1:2 के अनुपात में करने का निर्णय लिया। चिराग की सेवानिवृत्ति के दिन फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹ 5,40,000 किया गया ।
अधिलाभ अनुपात की गणना कीजिए तथा चिराग की सेवानिवृत्ति पर ख्याति का लेखा (ख्याति खाता खोले बिना) करने के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टि कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
Aamir, Bashir and Chirag were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3: 3: 2. Chirag retired. Aamir and Bashir decided to share profits and losses in future in the ratio of 1:2. On the day of Chirag's retirement, goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 5,40,000.
Calculate gaining ratio and pass necessary journal entry to record the treatment of goodwill (without opening goodwill account) on Chirag's retirement.

key_points: Old ratio is 3:3:2. New ratio is 1:2.
Gaining ratio calculation: Aamir = 1/3 - 3/8 = -1/24 (Sacrifice), Bashir = 2/3 - 3/8 = 7/24 (Gain).
Chirag's share of goodwill = 2/8 of 5,40,000 = 1,35,000.
Journal Entry: Bashir's Capital A/c Dr 1,57,500 To Aamir's Capital A/c 22,500 To Chirag's Capital A/c 1,35,000.

questions.solution: First, the gaining ratio is computed using the formula: Gaining Share = New Share - Old Share. For Aamir, it is 1/3 - 3/8 = -1/24, indicating he actually sacrifices a portion. For Bashir, it is 2/3 - 3/8 = 7/24, meaning he is the sole gaining partner. The total goodwill is valued at ₹5,40,000. Chirag, the retiring partner, must be compensated for his 2/8 share, which is ₹1,35,000. Additionally, Aamir must be compensated for his sacrifice of 1/24, equating to ₹22,500. Bashir will bear the total burden for his 7/24 gain, which equals ₹1,57,500. The required adjusting journal entry is to debit Bashir’s Capital Account by ₹1,57,500, and correspondingly credit Aamir’s Capital Account by ₹22,500 and Chirag’s Capital Account by ₹1,35,000, completing the goodwill adjustment cleanly.
questions.solution_hindi: सबसे पहले, अधिलाभ (Gaining) अनुपात की गणना की जाती है: नया हिस्सा - पुराना हिस्सा। आमीर के लिए, यह 1/3 - 3/8 = -1/24 है, जिसका अर्थ है कि वह वास्तव में त्याग कर रहा है। बशीर के लिए, यह 2/3 - 3/8 = 7/24 है, अर्थात वह एकमात्र लाभ प्राप्त करने वाला साझेदार है। ख्याति का कुल मूल्यांकन ₹5,40,000 है। सेवानिवृत्त होने वाले चिराग को उसके 2/8 हिस्से के लिए मुआवजा दिया जाएगा, जो ₹1,35,000 है। इसके अतिरिक्त, आमीर को उसके 1/24 के त्याग के लिए ₹22,500 का मुआवजा दिया जाना चाहिए। बशीर अपने 7/24 के लाभ के लिए ₹1,57,500 का संपूर्ण भार वहन करेगा। आवश्यक रोजनामचा प्रविष्टि में बशीर के पूंजी खाते को ₹1,57,500 से डेबिट किया जाएगा, और आमीर के पूंजी खाते को ₹22,500 तथा चिराग के पूंजी खाते को ₹1,35,000 से क्रेडिट किया जाएगा।

questions.text:
पर्ल तथा रुबी एक फर्म में साझेदार थीं तथा उनकी संयुक्त पूँजी ₹ 2,50,000 थी। प्रतिफल की सामान्य दर 10% थी। पिछले चार वर्षों के लाभ निम्न प्रकार थे :
2019-20 ₹ 35,000
2020-21 ₹ 25,000
2021-22 ₹ 32,000
2022-23 ₹ 33,000
वर्ष 2022 - 23 के अंतिम रहतिए (स्टॉक) का मूल्यांकन ₹ 5,000 अधिक किया गया । पिछले चार वर्षों के औसत अधिलाभ के तीन वर्षों के क्रय के आधार पर फर्म की ख्याति की गणना कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
Pearl and Ruby were partners in a firm with a combined capital of ₹ 2,50,000. The normal rate of return was 10%. The profits of the last four years were as follows:
2019-20 ₹ 35,000
2020-21 ₹ 25,000
2021-22 ₹ 32,000
2022-23 ₹ 33,000
The closing stock for the year 2022-23 was overvalued by ₹ 5,000. Calculate goodwill of the firm based on three years' purchase of the last four years' average super profit.

key_points: Normal Profit = 10% of 2,50,000 = 25,000.
Super Profit = Average Profit - Normal Profit = 30,000 - 25,000 = 5,000.
Goodwill = Super Profit × 3 = 15,000.

questions.solution: First, the normal profit of the firm is computed as 10% of the combined capital employed (₹2,50,000), yielding a normal profit of ₹25,000. Next, the profit for the year 2022-23 must be adjusted downwards to correct the ₹5,000 overvaluation of closing stock, rendering the corrected profit as ₹28,000. The average profit over the four years is then calculated by summing ₹35,000, ₹25,000, ₹32,000, and the adjusted ₹28,000 to get ₹1,20,000, which is then divided by 4 to establish an average actual profit of ₹30,000. The firm's super profit is the excess of average profit over normal profit, amounting to ₹5,000 (₹30,000 - ₹25,000). Finally, applying the three years' purchase method, the goodwill of the firm is firmly evaluated at ₹15,000.
questions.solution_hindi: सबसे पहले, फर्म का सामान्य लाभ नियोजित कुल पूंजी (₹2,50,000) का 10% आकलित किया जाता है, जो ₹25,000 होता है। इसके बाद, वर्ष 2022-23 के लाभ को अंतिम स्टॉक के ₹5,000 के अधिक मूल्यांकन को सही करने के लिए घटाया जाना चाहिए, जिससे समायोजित लाभ ₹28,000 हो जाता है। फिर चार वर्षों के औसत लाभ की गणना ₹35,000, ₹25,000, ₹32,000 और समायोजित ₹28,000 को जोड़कर ₹1,20,000 प्राप्त की जाती है, जिसे 4 से भाग देने पर ₹30,000 का औसत वास्तविक लाभ स्थापित होता है। फर्म का अधि-लाभ (Super profit) सामान्य लाभ से अधिक औसत लाभ है, जो ₹5,000 (₹30,000 - ₹25,000) है। अंत में, तीन वर्षों के क्रय के आधार पर, फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹15,000 किया जाएगा।

sub_questions.text: (क) सनराइज़ लिमिटेड ने मूनलाइट लिमिटेड से ₹4,80,000 के सहमत क्रय मूल्य पर ₹ 3,60,000 की परिसम्पत्तियों तथा ₹ 1,00,000 के लेनदारों का अधिग्रहण किया । क्रय मूल्य के भुगतान स्वरूप सनराइज़ लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 9% ऋणपत्रों का 4% बट्टे पर निर्गमन किया । सनराइज़ लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए । अपने कार्य को स्पष्टता से दर्शाइए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Sunrise Ltd. acquired assets of ₹ 3,60,000 and took over creditors of ₹ 1,00,000 from Moonlight Ltd. for an agreed purchase consideration of ₹ 4,80,000. Sunrise Ltd. issued 9% Debentures of ₹ 100 each at a discount of 4% in satisfaction of the purchase consideration. Pass necessary journal entries in the books of Sunrise Ltd. Show your workings clearly.

key_points: Goodwill calculation: Purchase Consideration (4,80,000) + Liabilities (1,00,000) - Assets (3,60,000) = Goodwill (2,20,000).
Entry 1: Assets A/c Dr 3,60,000, Goodwill A/c Dr 2,20,000 To Creditors A/c 1,00,000 To Moonlight Ltd 4,80,000.
Number of debentures to be issued = 4,80,000 / 96 = 5,000 debentures.
Entry 2: Moonlight Ltd Dr 4,80,000, Discount on Issue of Debentures A/c Dr 20,000 To 9% Debentures A/c 5,00,000.

sub_questions.solution: When Sunrise Ltd. acquired the business, the net assets taken over amounted to ₹2,60,000 (Assets of ₹3,60,000 minus Creditors of ₹1,00,000). Given the purchase consideration was agreed at ₹4,80,000, the excess amount paid of ₹2,20,000 is recognised as Goodwill. The first entry debits Assets (₹3,60,000) and Goodwill (₹2,20,000), and credits Creditors (₹1,00,000) and Moonlight Ltd. (₹4,80,000). For the payment, the debentures are issued at a 4% discount, making the issue price ₹96 per debenture. Dividing the liability of ₹4,80,000 by ₹96 reveals that exactly 5,000 debentures must be issued. The settlement entry will thus debit Moonlight Ltd. for ₹4,80,000, debit Discount on Issue of Debentures for ₹20,000, and heavily credit 9% Debentures Account for their full face value of ₹5,00,000.

sub_questions.text: (ख) ग्रेपल लिमिटेड ने ऐलोर लिमिटेड से ₹ 18,00,000 के सहमत क्रय मूल्य पर ₹ 25,00,000 की परिसम्पत्तियों तथा ₹ 5,00,000 की देयताओं का अधिग्रहण किया । क्रय मूल्य के भुगतान स्वरूप ग्रेपल लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 11% ऋणपत्रों को 20% प्रीमियम पर निर्गमन किया । ग्रेपल लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए । अपने कार्य को स्पष्टता से दर्शाइए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Grapple Ltd. took over assets of ₹ 25,00,000 and liabilities of ₹ 5,00,000 from Allore Ltd. for an agreed purchase consideration of ₹ 18,00,000. Grapple Ltd. issued 11% Debentures of ₹ 100 each at 20% premium in satisfaction of the purchase consideration. Pass necessary journal entries in the books of Grapple Ltd. Show your workings clearly.

key_points: Capital Reserve calculation: Assets (25,00,000) - Liabilities (5,00,000) - Purchase Consideration (18,00,000) = Capital Reserve (2,00,000).
Entry 1: Assets A/c Dr 25,00,000 To Liabilities A/c 5,00,000 To Allore Ltd 18,00,000 To Capital Reserve A/c 2,00,000.
Number of debentures to be issued = 18,00,000 / 120 = 15,000 debentures.
Entry 2: Allore Ltd Dr 18,00,000 To 11% Debentures A/c 15,00,000 To Securities Premium Reserve A/c 3,00,000.

sub_questions.solution: Upon taking over the business from Allore Ltd., Grapple Ltd. received net assets worth ₹20,00,000 (Assets of ₹25,00,000 minus Liabilities of ₹5,00,000). Since the purchase consideration was aggressively negotiated down to just ₹18,00,000, the remaining ₹2,00,000 represents a clear capital profit and is transferred to the Capital Reserve. The first entry debits Assets for ₹25,00,000, and credits Liabilities (₹5,00,000), Allore Ltd. (₹18,00,000), and Capital Reserve (₹2,00,000). For the discharge of purchase consideration, debentures are issued at a 20% premium, resulting in an issue price of ₹120 each. Dividing ₹18,00,000 by ₹120 gives exactly 15,000 debentures. The payment entry cleanly debits Allore Ltd. for ₹18,00,000, and credits 11% Debentures for ₹15,00,000 alongside a credit to Securities Premium Reserve for the ₹3,00,000 premium collected.

sub_questions.text: (क) मोहन, सुहान तथा अदित एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 3:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । उनकी स्थायी पूँजी क्रमशः ₹ 2,00,000, ₹ 1,00,000 तथा ₹ 1,00,000 थी । 31 मार्च, 2023 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष में उनके खाते में पूँजी पर ब्याज 5% वार्षिक दर की अपेक्षा 8% वार्षिक दर से जमा कर दिया गया । आवश्यक समायोजन रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टि कीजिए। अपने कार्य को स्पष्टता से दर्शाइए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Mohan, Suhaan and Adit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2:1. Their fixed capitals were: ₹ 2,00,000, ₹ 1,00,000 and ₹ 1,00,000 respectively. For the year ended 31st March, 2023, interest on capital was credited to their accounts @ 8% p.a. instead of 5% p.a. Pass necessary adjusting journal entry. Show your workings clearly.

key_points: Excess interest credited = 3% p.a. (Mohan 6,000, Suhaan 3,000, Adit 3,000). Total excess = 12,000.
This 12,000 represents profit that should have been distributed in 3:2:1 ratio (Mohan 6,000, Suhaan 4,000, Adit 2,000).
Net effect: Mohan (Dr 6,000, Cr 6,000 = Nil). Suhaan (Dr 3,000, Cr 4,000 = Cr 1,000). Adit (Dr 3,000, Cr 2,000 = Dr 1,000).
Entry is passed through Current Accounts as capitals are fixed.
Entry: Adit's Current A/c Dr 1,000 To Suhaan's Current A/c 1,000.

sub_questions.solution: The partners were incorrectly credited with 8% interest on capital instead of the required 5%, resulting in an excess credit of 3%. The excess interest wrongfully credited to their accounts is ₹6,000 for Mohan, ₹3,000 for Suhaan, and ₹3,000 for Adit, aggregating to ₹12,000. This ₹12,000 should have been standard profit and distributed in their correct profit-sharing ratio of 3:2:1, which equates to right credits of ₹6,000 to Mohan, ₹4,000 to Suhaan, and ₹2,000 to Adit. Contrasting the wrongful credits against the rightful ones reveals Mohan's balance is unaffected, Suhaan should be credited an additional ₹1,000, and Adit must be debited by ₹1,000. Since capitals are explicitly stated as fixed, current accounts are strictly used. The final adjustment entry will debit Adit’s Current Account for ₹1,000 and logically credit Suhaan’s Current Account for ₹1,000.

sub_questions.text: (ख) मनोज एवं नितिन एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । 31 मार्च, 2023 को लाभ एवं आहरण का समायोजन करने के पश्चात् उनके पूँजी खातों का शेष क्रमशः ₹90,000 तथा ₹ 80,000 था । 31 मार्च, 2023 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए शुद्ध लाभ की राशि ₹ 30,000 थी । वर्ष के दौरान मनोज ने ₹ 40,000 तथा नितिन ने ₹ 20,000 का आहरण किया । बाद में, ध्यान दिया गया कि साझेदारों को 10% वार्षिक दर से पूँजी पर ब्याज नहीं दिया गया था । मनोज के आहरण पर ₹3,000 तथा नितिन के आहरण पर ₹ 2,000 का ब्याज भी प्रभारित नहीं किया गया था । आवश्यक समायोजन रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टि कीजिए। अपने कार्य को स्पष्टता से दर्शाइए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Manoj and Nitin were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:1. On 31st March, 2023, the balances in their capital accounts after making adjustments for profits and drawings were ₹ 90,000 and ₹ 80,000 respectively. The net profit for the year ended 31st March, 2023 amounted to ₹ 30,000. During the year Manoj withdrew ₹ 40,000 and Nitin withdrew ₹ 20,000. Subsequently, it was noticed that Interest on Capital @ 10% p.a. was not provided to the partners. Also Interest on Drawings to Manoj ₹ 3,000 and to Nitin ₹ 2,000 was not charged. Pass necessary adjusting journal entry. Show your workings clearly.

key_points: Calculation of Opening Capital: Closing Capital + Drawings - Share of Profit (30,000 in 2:1 ratio).
Interest on Capital @ 10%: Manoj = 11,000; Nitin = 9,000. Total = 20,000.
Correct Divisible Profit = Original Profit (30,000) - IOC (20,000) + IOD (5,000) = 15,000 (Manoj 10,000; Nitin 5,000).
Already credited: Manoj = 20,000; Nitin = 10,000.
Net effect: Manoj is debited by 2,000, Nitin is credited by 2,000.
Entry: Manoj's Capital A/c Dr 2,000 To Nitin's Capital A/c 2,000.

sub_questions.solution: First, the opening capitals must be calculated to compute interest accurately. Adding back drawings and subtracting the wrongly distributed ₹30,000 profit (distributed in 2:1) yields opening capitals of ₹1,10,000 for Manoj and ₹90,000 for Nitin. The rightful 10% Interest on Capital is ₹11,000 for Manoj and ₹9,000 for Nitin, totaling ₹20,000. Including Interest on Drawings (₹5,000), the correctly adjusted divisible profit is ₹15,000 (₹30,000 - ₹20,000 + ₹5,000), giving Manoj ₹10,000 and Nitin ₹5,000. Therefore, the absolute correct credits they should have received for the year are ₹18,000 for Manoj (₹11k IOC - ₹3k IOD + ₹10k profit) and ₹12,000 for Nitin (₹9k IOC - ₹2k IOD + ₹5k profit). Because they were wrongly credited ₹20,000 and ₹10,000 respectively, Manoj was over-credited by ₹2,000 and Nitin was under-credited by ₹2,000. The precise adjusting entry debits Manoj's Capital Account for ₹2,000 and credits Nitin's Capital Account for ₹2,000.

questions.text:
शिवालिक लिमिटेड ₹10 प्रत्येक के समता अंशों / शेयरों में विभाजित ₹ 10,00,000 की अधिकृत पूँजी के साथ पंजीकृत थी । इसने जनता को 50,000 समता अंशों/शेयरों के लिए प्रस्ताव दिया । राशि का भुगतान निम्न प्रकार से करना था :
आवेदन पर ₹2 प्रति अंश/शेयर
आबंटन पर ₹6 प्रति अंश/शेयर
प्रथम एवं अंतिम याचना पर शेष
निर्गमन पूर्ण रूप से अभिदत्त हुआ । केवल 4,000 समता अंशों/शेयरों पर आबंटन तथा प्रथम एवं अंतिम याचना राशि को छोड़कर सभी देय राशियाँ विधिवत् प्राप्त कर लीं गईं। इन समता अंशों/शेयरों का हरण कर लिया गया ।
कम्पनी अधिनियम, 2013 की अनुसूची III, भाग I के अनुसार कम्पनी के स्थिति विवरण में अंश/शेयर पूँजी को दर्शाइए । इसके लिए 'खातों के नोट्स' भी तैयार कीजिए ।

Shivalik Limited was registered with an authorized capital of ₹ 10,00,000 divided into equity shares of ₹ 10 each. It offered 50,000 equity shares to the public. The amount was payable as follows:
On Application ₹ 2 per share
On Allotment ₹ 6 per share
On First and Final call Balance
The issue was fully subscribed. All the amounts were duly received except the allotment and first and final call money on 4,000 equity shares. These equity shares were forfeited.
Present the Share Capital in the Balance Sheet of the company as per Schedule III, Part I of the Companies Act, 2013. Also prepare 'Notes to Accounts' for the same.

key_points: Authorized Capital: 1,00,000 Equity shares of ₹10 each = ₹10,00,000.
Issued Capital: 50,000 Equity shares of ₹10 each = ₹5,00,000.
Subscribed Capital: 46,000 Equity shares of ₹10 each fully paid up = ₹4,60,000.
Add: Share Forfeiture Account (4,000 shares × ₹2 received on application) = ₹8,000.
Total Share Capital to be shown in the Balance Sheet = ₹4,68,000.

questions.solution: In the Notes to Accounts under 'Share Capital', the Authorized Capital is presented first as 1,00,000 Equity Shares of ₹10 each, amounting to ₹10,00,000. This is followed by the Issued Capital of 50,000 Equity Shares of ₹10 each, equal to ₹5,00,000. For Subscribed Capital, since 4,000 shares were completely forfeited and not reissued, the 'Subscribed and Fully Paid up' category will show only 46,000 Equity Shares of ₹10 each, totaling ₹4,60,000. Additionally, the amount retained by the company on the 4,000 forfeited shares (the ₹2 application money paid) must be added. This ₹8,000 is placed under 'Add: Share Forfeiture Account'. Therefore, the final total of Share Capital to be strictly extracted to the main Balance Sheet under the 'Equity and Liabilities' segment is accurately recorded as ₹4,68,000.
questions.solution_hindi: खातों के नोट्स (Notes to Accounts) में 'अंश पूंजी' के अंतर्गत, अधिकृत पूंजी को पहले ₹10 प्रत्येक के 1,00,000 समता अंशों के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया जाता है, जो ₹10,00,000 है। इसके बाद ₹10 प्रत्येक के 50,000 समता अंशों की निर्गमित पूंजी, जो ₹5,00,000 के बराबर है। अभिदत्त पूंजी के लिए, चूंकि 4,000 अंशों को पूरी तरह से हरण कर लिया गया था और पुनः निर्गमित नहीं किया गया था, इसलिए 'अभिदत्त और पूर्ण प्रदत्त' श्रेणी में केवल 46,000 समता अंश ₹10 प्रत्येक के दिखाए जाएंगे, जो कुल ₹4,60,000 है। इसके अतिरिक्त, कंपनी द्वारा 4,000 हरण किए गए अंशों पर रखी गई राशि (भुगतान की गई ₹2 आवेदन राशि) को जोड़ा जाना चाहिए। इस ₹8,000 को 'जोड़ें: अंश हरण खाता' के तहत रखा जाता है। इसलिए, 'समता और देयताएं' खंड के तहत मुख्य स्थिति विवरण में सटीक रूप से दर्शाए जाने वाले अंश पूंजी का अंतिम योग ₹4,68,000 दर्ज किया जाता है।

Archana, Vandana and Arti were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3:2. Their Balance Sheet on 31st March, 2023 was as follows:

| Liabilities | Amount (₹) | Assets | Amount (₹) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Capitals: Archana | 80,000 | Investments | 80,000 |
| Vandana | 70,000 | Plant | 1,00,000 |
| Arti | 60,000 | Stock | 40,000 |
| General Reserve | 30,000 | Debtors | 50,000 |
| Creditors | 60,000 | Cash at Bank | 30,000 |
| Total | 3,00,000 | Total | 3,00,000 |

The firm was dissolved on the above date.
(i) Assets were realised as follows: Debtors ₹ 40,000, Stock ₹ 50,000, Plant ₹ 60,000
(ii) 25% of the Investments were taken over by Vandana at ₹ 18,000. Remaining Investments were taken over by Archana at 10% less than its book value.
(iii) Expenses of realisation ₹ 20,000 were paid by Arti.
Prepare Realisation Account.

key_points: Transfer of Assets to debit side: Investments (80,000), Plant (1,00,000), Stock (40,000), Debtors (50,000) = Total 2,70,000.
Transfer of Liabilities to credit side: Creditors (60,000).
Assets realized credited to Bank: Debtors (40k) + Stock (50k) + Plant (60k) = 1,50,000.
Investments taken over: Vandana's Cap A/c (18,000), Archana's Cap A/c (60,000 - 10% = 54,000).
Payment of Liabilities (implied full): Bank A/c Dr 60,000.
Expenses paid by Arti: Arti's Cap A/c Dr 20,000 on the debit side.
Realisation Loss calculation: Total Debit (3,50,000) - Total Credit (2,82,000) = 68,000.
Distribution of Loss in 5:3:2: Archana (34,000), Vandana (20,400), Arti (13,600).

questions.solution: The Realisation Account handles all asset closures and settlement of liabilities. On the debit side, all non-cash assets are transferred at book value: Investments (₹80,000), Plant (₹1,00,000), Stock (₹40,000), and Debtors (₹50,000), totalling ₹2,70,000. Creditors are transferred to the credit side at ₹60,000. Cash realised from assets (Debtors, Stock, and Plant) amounts to ₹1,50,000, credited via the Bank account. For investments, 25% (₹20,000 book value) are taken by Vandana for ₹18,000. The remaining 75% (₹60,000 book value) are taken by Archana at a 10% discount, yielding ₹54,000; both are credited appropriately to their Capital Accounts. The liabilities (Creditors) are paid in full for ₹60,000 on the debit side, and Arti is credited ₹20,000 for assuming the realisation expenses. Summing the debit side (₹3,50,000) and subtracting the credit side (₹2,82,000) reveals a definitive net Realisation Loss of ₹68,000. This loss is distributed among Archana (₹34,000), Vandana (₹20,400), and Arti (₹13,600) strictly in their profit-sharing ratio of 5:3:2.
questions.solution_hindi: वसूली खाता (Realisation Account) सभी परिसंपत्तियों को बंद करने और देनदारियों के निपटान को संभालता है। डेबिट पक्ष पर, सभी गैर-नकद संपत्तियों को पुस्तक मूल्य पर स्थानांतरित किया जाता है: निवेश (₹80,000), संयंत्र (₹1,00,000), स्टॉक (₹40,000), और देनदार (₹50,000), कुल ₹2,70,000। लेनदारों को क्रेडिट पक्ष में ₹60,000 पर स्थानांतरित किया जाता है। परिसंपत्तियों (देनदार, स्टॉक, संयंत्र) से प्राप्त नकद ₹1,50,000 है, जिसे बैंक खाते के माध्यम से क्रेडिट किया जाता है। निवेश के लिए, 25% (₹20,000 पुस्तक मूल्य) वंदना द्वारा ₹18,000 में लिया जाता है। शेष 75% (₹60,000 पुस्तक मूल्य) अर्चना द्वारा 10% छूट पर लिया जाता है, जो ₹54,000 है; दोनों को उनके पूंजी खातों में क्रेडिट किया जाता है। लेनदारों का डेबिट पक्ष पर ₹60,000 का पूर्ण भुगतान किया जाता है, और वसूली व्यय के लिए आरती को ₹20,000 का क्रेडिट दिया जाता है। डेबिट पक्ष (₹3,50,000) को जोड़ने और क्रेडिट पक्ष (₹2,82,000) को घटाने पर ₹68,000 की शुद्ध वसूली हानि का पता चलता है। यह हानि अर्चना (₹34,000), वंदना (₹20,400), और आरती (₹13,600) के बीच 5:3:2 के अनुपात में वितरित की जाती है।

Azhar, Sumit and Robit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:1: 1. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2023, was as follows:

| Liabilities | Amount ₹ | Assets | Amount ₹ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Creditors | 90,000 | Bank | 20,000 |
| General Reserve | 60,000 | Stock | 40,000 |
| Capitals: Azhar | 60,000 | Debtors | 1,50,000 |
| Sumit | 40,000 | Fixed Assets | 60,000 |
| Robit | 20,000 | |
| Total | 2,70,000 | Total | 2,70,000 |

Robit died on 30th June, 2023. According to the Partnership deed, Robit's legal representatives were entitled to :
(i) Balance in his Capital Account.
(ii) His share of General Reserve.
(iii) Interest on capital @ 10% p.a.
(iv) His share of goodwill. Goodwill of the firm was valued on the basis of thrice the average of the past four years' profits.
(v) His share in profits up to the date of death on the basis of the profit for the last year.
Profit for the previous years were :
2019-20: ₹ (3,000)
2020-21: ₹ 28,000
2021-22: ₹ 16,000
2022-23: ₹ 15,000
Prepare Robit's Capital Account to be rendered to his legal representatives.

key_points: Credit balance brought down: ₹20,000.
Share of General Reserve: 1/5th of 60,000 = ₹12,000.
Interest on Capital: 20,000 × 10% × (3/12) months = ₹500.
Calculation of Goodwill: Average Profit = (-3k + 28k + 16k + 15k)/4 = 14k. Goodwill = 14k × 3 = 42k. Robit's share = 42,000 × 1/5 = ₹8,400.
Share of Profit up to death: Last year profit (15k) × (3/12) months × (1/5) share = ₹750 (credited via P&L Suspense).
Total credit side of Robit's Capital A/c = 20,000 + 12,000 + 500 + 8,400 + 750 = ₹41,650.
Transfer balance of ₹41,650 to Robit's Executors Account.

questions.solution: Robit's Capital Account requires assembling multiple components to determine the final amount due to his legal representatives. Starting on the credit side, the opening capital balance is ₹20,000. Next, Robit receives his 1/5th share of the ₹60,000 General Reserve, amounting to ₹12,000. He survived for three months in the current accounting year (up to 30th June), entitling him to 3 months' Interest on Capital, calculated as ₹20,000 × 10% × 3/12, which equals ₹500. To ascertain his share of goodwill, the four-year average profit is computed as (-3,000 + 28,000 + 16,000 + 15,000) divided by 4, yielding an average profit of ₹14,000. Firm goodwill is thus ₹42,000 (14k × 3), and Robit’s 1/5th share comes to ₹8,400. This is borne by Azhar and Sumit in their gaining ratio (3:1). Finally, his share of profit up to death is based strictly on the previous year's ₹15,000 profit, equating to ₹15,000 × 3/12 × 1/5 = ₹750, handled via a P&L Suspense Account. The grand total of these credits is ₹41,650, which is then fully transferred to Robit's Executors Account on the debit side to close the ledger.
questions.solution_hindi: रोबित के पूंजी खाते में उसके कानूनी प्रतिनिधियों को देय अंतिम राशि निर्धारित करने के लिए कई घटकों को एकत्र करने की आवश्यकता है। क्रेडिट पक्ष से शुरू करते हुए, प्रारंभिक पूंजी शेष ₹20,000 है। इसके बाद, रोबित को ₹60,000 के सामान्य संचय का अपना 1/5 वां हिस्सा प्राप्त होता है, जो ₹12,000 है। वह चालू लेखा वर्ष में तीन महीने (30 जून तक) जीवित रहा, जिससे वह 3 महीने की पूंजी पर ब्याज का हकदार हो गया, जिसकी गणना ₹20,000 × 10% × 3/12 के रूप में की गई, जो ₹500 के बराबर है। उसकी ख्याति का हिस्सा सुनिश्चित करने के लिए, चार साल के औसत लाभ की गणना (-3,000 + 28,000 + 16,000 + 15,000) को 4 से भाग देकर की जाती है, जिससे ₹14,000 का औसत लाभ प्राप्त होता है। इस प्रकार फर्म की ख्याति ₹42,000 (14k × 3) है, और रोबित का 1/5 वां हिस्सा ₹8,400 आता है। इसे अज़हर और सुमित द्वारा उनके अधिलाभ अनुपात (3:1) में वहन किया जाता है। अंत में, मृत्यु तक के लाभ का उसका हिस्सा पिछले वर्ष के ₹15,000 के लाभ पर आधारित है, जो ₹15,000 × 3/12 × 1/5 = ₹750 के बराबर है, जिसे P&L सस्पेंस खाते के माध्यम से नियंत्रित किया जाता है। इन क्रेडिट का कुल योग ₹41,650 है, जिसे रोबित के निष्पादक (Executors) खाते में पूरी तरह से स्थानांतरित कर दिया जाता है।

(a) Pass necessary journal entries for issue of debentures and for writing off 'Loss on Issue of Debentures' utilising Securities Premium Account at the end of the first year itself.
(b) Prepare 'Loss on Issue of Debentures Account' for the year ended 31st March, 2023.

key_points: (a) Issue entry 1: Bank A/c Dr 10,60,000 To Debenture App & Allotment A/c 10,60,000.

(b) Loss on Issue of Debentures Account: Debit side: 'To Premium on Redemption A/c' 40,000. Credit side: 'By Securities Premium Reserve A/c' 40,000. Account is closed.

questions.solution: The face value of the debentures issued is ₹10,00,000. The debentures were issued at a 6% premium, which means the company collected ₹60,000 as Securities Premium. The first entry debits Bank and credits Debenture Application & Allotment for ₹10,60,000. Since they are redeemable at a 4% premium, a future liability of ₹40,000 is recognized immediately as a 'Loss on Issue of Debentures'. The allotment entry effectively debits Debenture App & Allotment for ₹10,60,000 and Loss on Issue for ₹40,000, while crediting 7% Debentures (₹10,00,000), Securities Premium Reserve (₹60,000), and Premium on Redemption (₹40,000). To write off the loss, the available SPR balance is verified: ₹30,000 existing plus ₹60,000 collected equals ₹90,000, easily covering the ₹40,000 loss. The write-off entry purely debits SPR and credits Loss on Issue for ₹40,000. The Loss on Issue Account simply reflects these entries: a debit posted as 'To Premium on Redemption of Debentures ₹40,000' and an identical credit posted as 'By Securities Premium Reserve ₹40,000', squarely balancing the ledger account.

(a) Qumtan Ltd. invited applications for issuing 1,00,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each at a premium of 6 per share. The amount was payable as follows:
On Application and Allotment ₹ 8 per share (including premium ₹ 3)
On First and Final call Balance (including premium)
Applications for 1,60,000 shares were received. Applications for 10,000 shares were rejected and pro-rata allotment was made to the remaining applicants. Excess money received on application and allotment was returned. Dheeraj, who was allotted 200 shares, failed to pay the first and final call money. His shares were forfeited. All the forfeited shares were reissued at ₹ 5 per share fully paid up. Pass necessary journal entries in the books of Qumtan Ltd.

key_points: Issue price is 16. App & Allot is 8 (Cap 5, Prem 3). Call is 8 (Cap 5, Prem 3).
1,60,000 applied. 10,000 rejected (80,000 refunded). Remaining 1,50,000 applied allotted 1,00,000 (ratio 3:2).

Dheeraj allotted 200 shares. Since excess money was fully returned (as it says 'excess money received on application and allotment was returned'), no excess money was adjusted to calls for any shareholder.
Call arrears for Dheeraj: 200 * 8 = 1,600.
Forfeiture Entry: Share Capital Dr (200*10 = 2,000), SPR Dr (200*3 = 600) To Share Forfeiture A/c (200*5 = 1,000) To Calls in Arrears (1,600).
Reissue Entry: Bank A/c Dr (200*5 = 1,000), Share Forfeiture A/c Dr 1,000 To Share Capital A/c 2,000.
Transfer to Capital Reserve = Nil (since all 1,000 in forfeiture account was used as discount).

sub_questions.solution: The share's issue price is ₹16 (₹10 face + ₹6 premium). The breakdown is exactly ₹8 on Application & Allotment (Capital ₹5, Premium ₹3) and the remaining ₹8 on Call (Capital ₹5, Premium ₹3). The company received ₹12,80,000 for 1,60,000 shares. It outright rejected 10,000 applications, meaning ₹80,000 was refunded. The pro-rata was completed on the remaining 1,50,000 applications for 1,00,000 shares. Crucially, the problem clearly states that the excess money received on application and allotment was entirely returned. This means the surplus ₹4,00,000 from the pro-rata applicants was completely refunded, rather than carried forward to the call. Therefore, total refunds amount to ₹4,80,000. Consequently, Dheeraj, who was allotted 200 shares, possessed no surplus money adjusted towards his call. He failed to pay the entire ₹8 call (including ₹3 premium). His shares were forfeited by debiting Share Capital for ₹2,000 (200×10) and SPR for ₹600 (the unpaid premium). The credit goes to Share Forfeiture for the capital amount he paid (₹1,000) and Calls in Arrears for ₹1,600. Upon reissuing all 200 shares at ₹5, a discount of ₹5 per share is allowed, which completely utilizes the ₹1,000 resting in the Share Forfeiture account. As a result, no balance remains to be transferred to the Capital Reserve account.

(b) Printkit Limited invited applications for issue of 80,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each. The amount was payable as follows:

On Allotment - ₹ 2 per share
On First and Final call Balance
Applications for 1,50,000 shares were received. Applications for 10,000 shares were rejected and pro-rata allotment was made to the remaining applicants on the following basis:
Category A Applicants for 80,000 shares were allotted 40,000 shares.
Category B Applicants for 60,000 shares were allotted 40,000 shares.
Excess money received on application was adjusted towards amount due on allotment and first and final call. All the amounts due on allotment and first and final call were duly received. Pass necessary journal entries in the books of Printkit Limited.

key_points: Total application money received: 1,50,000 × 3 = 4,50,000.
Capital requirement: 80,000 × 3 = 2,40,000. Refund for rejected: 10,000 × 3 = 30,000.
Category A excess: (80k - 40k) × 3 = 1,20,000. Allotment due is 40k × 2 = 80,000. Excess 40,000 goes to Calls in Advance.
Category B excess: (60k - 40k) × 3 = 60,000. Allotment due is 40k × 2 = 80,000. All 60,000 adjusted on allotment.
Total adjusted to Allotment = 80,000 + 60,000 = 1,40,000. Total adjusted to Calls in Advance = 40,000.
First & Final Call due = 80,000 × 5 = 4,00,000. Received = 4,00,000 - 40,000 (advance) = 3,60,000.

sub_questions.solution: The company invited applications for 80,000 shares. Total application money received was ₹4,50,000 (1,50,000 shares × ₹3). Out of this, ₹30,000 is immediately refunded for the 10,000 rejected shares. The application capital amount transferred is ₹2,40,000 (80,000 × ₹3). We then analyze the pro-rata categories to handle the excess application money properly. For Category A (80k applied, 40k allotted), the excess money received is 40,000 × ₹3 = ₹1,20,000. The allotment due for Category A is only 40,000 × ₹2 = ₹80,000. Thus, ₹80,000 is adjusted towards allotment, and the remaining ₹40,000 is transferred forward to Calls in Advance. For Category B (60k applied, 40k allotted), the excess is 20,000 × ₹3 = ₹60,000. Since their allotment due is ₹80,000, the entire ₹60,000 excess is fully consumed by the allotment. Therefore, the total amount adjusted to Share Allotment is ₹1,40,000 (80k + 60k), and ₹40,000 moves to Calls in Advance. The allotment money actually received in the bank is the total due (₹1,60,000) minus the adjusted sum (₹1,40,000), leaving just ₹20,000. Finally, the First and Final Call due is ₹4,00,000 (80,000 shares × ₹5). Adjusting the previously held ₹40,000 from Calls in Advance, the exact bank receipt on the final call is ₹3,60,000. Complete journal entries reflect these calculated movements progressively.

The net revaluation loss is ₹20,000, which is distributed in the 3:2 old ratio, debiting Shubhi for ₹12,000 and Revanshi for ₹8,000. In the Partners' Capital Accounts, opening balances are ₹60,000 and ₹32,000 respectively. The General Reserve of ₹30,000 is distributed (3:2), crediting them ₹18,000 and ₹12,000. Capital adjustment is determined based on Pari's ₹50,000 for a 1/4th share, making the total firm capital ₹2,00,000. The new profit-sharing ratio equates to 9:6:5, demanding new closing capitals of ₹90,000 for Shubhi and ₹60,000 for Revanshi. Comparing the adjusted capitals against the required balances dictates that Shubhi has an excess of ₹6,000 which she will withdraw in cash, while Revanshi has a deficit of ₹4,000, requiring her to bring in that exact cash amount.

Shashi retired from the firm on 1st April, 2023 on the following terms:

(iv) Balance in Shashi's Capital Account was transferred to her loan account.
Prepare Revaluation Account and Partners' Capital Accounts.

key_points: Revaluation Account: Fixed Assets reduced by 24,000. Stock increased by 6,000 (taken over at 26,000). Net Loss = 18,000. Distributed 3:1:2 (Rishi 9,000, Shashi 3,000, Trishi 6,000).
Goodwill adjustment: Firm goodwill 18k. Shashi's share = 3,000. Gaining ratio of Rishi and Trishi is 3:2. Rishi Dr 1,800, Trishi Dr 1,200 To Shashi 3,000.

However, Stock exhibits an appreciation of ₹6,000 (since Shashi takes it over at ₹26,000 compared to a book value of ₹20,000). This results in a net revaluation loss of ₹18,000, distributed as ₹9,000 to Rishi, ₹3,000 to Shashi, and ₹6,000 to Trishi. The firm's total goodwill is ₹18,000, giving retiring Shashi a share of ₹3,000. Rishi and Trishi, gaining in their continuous ratio of 3:2, will compensate Shashi by debiting their capital accounts for ₹1,800 and ₹1,200 respectively. (b) Loose Tools: Major Head - Current Assets, Sub-head - Inventories.

questions.solution: According to Schedule III Part I of the Companies Act, 2013, the items are accurately classified as follows. Firstly, 'Long Term Loans from Bank' fall firmly under the Major Head of 'Non-Current Liabilities', with their specific Sub-head being 'Long-term Borrowings'. Secondly, 'Loose Tools' are universally classified beneath the Major Head of 'Current Assets', specifically categorized under the Sub-head 'Inventories'. Finally, 'Outstanding Expenses' sit under the Major Head of 'Current Liabilities' and are detailed within the Sub-head 'Other Current Liabilities'.

(b) Inventory Turnover Ratio

| Particulars | Amount (₹) |
|---|---|
| Current Assets | 4,00,000 |
| Inventory | 1,00,000 |
| Current Liabilities | 2,00,000 |
| Net Profit Before Tax | 7,20,000 |
| Revenue from Operations | 10,00,000 |
| Gross Profit Ratio 20% | |

key_points: (a) Quick Assets = Current Assets - Inventory = 4,00,000 - 1,00,000 = 3,00,000.
(a) Quick Ratio = Quick Assets / Current Liabilities = 3,00,000 / 2,00,000 = 1.5 : 1.
(b) Gross Profit = 20% of Revenue from Operations (10,00,000) = 2,00,000.
(b) Cost of Revenue from Operations (COGS) = Revenue from Operations - Gross Profit = 10,00,000 - 2,00,000 = 8,00,000.
(b) Inventory Turnover Ratio = COGS / Average Inventory (using given Inventory as average) = 8,00,000 / 1,00,000 = 8 Times.

questions.solution: To calculate the Quick Ratio, we first extract the Quick Assets by completely subtracting Inventory from Current Assets (₹4,00,000 - ₹1,00,000), which yields ₹3,00,000. Dividing Quick Assets (₹3,00,000) by Current Liabilities (₹2,00,000) provides a definitive Quick Ratio of 1.5:1. For the Inventory Turnover Ratio, the Gross Profit must first be determined as 20% of the Revenue from Operations, amounting to ₹2,00,000 (20% of ₹10,00,000). The Cost of Revenue from Operations (COGS) naturally follows by subtracting Gross Profit from the Revenue, giving ₹8,00,000. Finally, utilizing the available Inventory data point as the average, the Inventory Turnover Ratio is computed as ₹8,00,000 divided by ₹1,00,000, establishing a robust result of 8 times.

questions.text_english:
From the following information, calculate 'Cash Flows From Operating Activities':

| Particulars | Amount (₹) |
|---|---|
| Surplus i.e. Balance in Statement of Profit and Loss | 6,28,000 |
| Provision for Tax | 1,50,000 |
| Proposed Dividend for the previous year | 72,000 |
| Depreciation | 1,40,000 |
| Loss on Sale of Machinery | 30,000 |
| Gain on Sale of Investments | 20,000 |
| Dividend Received on Investments | 6,000 |
| Increase in Current Liabilities | 1,61,000 |
| Increase in Current Assets (other than cash and cash equivalents) | 6,00,000 |
| Decrease in Current Liabilities | 64,000 |
| Income Tax Paid | 1,18,000 |

key_points: Net Profit Before Tax & Extraordinary Items = Surplus (6,28,000) + Provision for Tax (1,50,000) + Proposed Div (72,000) = 8,50,000.
Add non-cash/non-operating charges: Depreciation (1,40,000) + Loss on sale (30,000) = 1,70,000.
Less non-operating incomes: Gain on sale (20,000) + Dividend received (6,000) = 26,000.
Operating Profit before Working Capital changes = 8,50,000 + 1,70,000 - 26,000 = 9,94,000.
Working Capital Adjustments: Add Increase in CL (1,61,000), Less Decrease in CL (64,000), Less Increase in CA (6,00,000).
Cash generated from operations = 9,94,000 + 1,61,000 - 6,64,000 = 4,91,000.
Less Income Tax Paid (1,18,000).
Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities = 3,73,000.

questions.solution: The computation commences by decisively establishing the Net Profit before Tax and Extraordinary Items. Taking the baseline Surplus of ₹6,28,000, we add back the current year's Provision for Tax (₹1,50,000) and the Proposed Dividend for the previous year (₹72,000), escalating the profit base to ₹8,50,000. To ascertain the Operating Profit prior to working capital changes, non-cash and non-operating debits like Depreciation (₹1,40,000) and Loss on Sale of Machinery (₹30,000) are added back. Simultaneously, non-operating credits such as Gain on Sale of Investments (₹20,000) and Dividend Received (₹6,000) are rigorously deducted. This establishes an operating base of ₹9,94,000. Evaluating the working capital, we strictly add the increase in Current Liabilities (₹1,61,000), while heavily deducting the increase in Current Assets (₹6,00,000) and the decrease in Current Liabilities (₹64,000). This arithmetic yields Cash Generated from Operations of ₹4,91,000. Finally, subtracting the actual Income Tax Paid of ₹1,18,000 produces a robust positive Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities definitively standing at ₹3,73,000.

questions.text_english: Explain the terms 'Doughnut' and 'Exploded Doughnut' as types of charts.

key_points: Doughnut Chart: Similar to a pie chart, displays data in rings, allows multiple data series to be plotted.
Exploded Doughnut Chart: It is a variant of the doughnut chart where individual slices are pulled out or separated from the center to emphasize specific data points.

questions.solution: A Doughnut chart is conceptually similar to a traditional pie chart as it illustrates the relationship of distinct parts to a whole. However, unlike a pie chart, a doughnut chart elegantly contains more than a single data series, presenting them in concentric rings with a characteristic blank center. An Exploded Doughnut chart is a direct aesthetic variation of the standard doughnut chart. In this specific format, the individual categorical slices are pulled away or separated from the core center. This explosion effect is deliberately used to visually highlight and draw the viewer's attention to specific, significant data points within the chart.
questions.solution_hindi: डोनट चार्ट (Doughnut Chart) अवधारणात्मक रूप से एक पारंपरिक पाई चार्ट के समान है क्योंकि यह एक संपूर्ण के विशिष्ट भागों के संबंध को दर्शाता है। हालांकि, पाई चार्ट के विपरीत, एक डोनट चार्ट में एक से अधिक डेटा श्रृंखलाएं शामिल हो सकती हैं, जो उन्हें एक विशिष्ट खाली केंद्र के साथ गाढ़ा छल्ले (concentric rings) में प्रस्तुत करती हैं। एक विस्फोटित डोनट (Exploded Doughnut) चार्ट मानक डोनट चार्ट की प्रत्यक्ष सौंदर्य भिन्नता है। इस विशिष्ट प्रारूप में, व्यक्तिगत स्लाइस को मूल केंद्र से दूर खींचा या अलग किया जाता है। इस विस्फोट प्रभाव का उपयोग जानबूझकर चार्ट के भीतर विशिष्ट, महत्वपूर्ण डेटा बिंदुओं को उजागर करने और दर्शक का ध्यान आकर्षित करने के लिए किया जाता है।

questions.text_english: Explain 'Transparency and Control' and 'Accuracy and Speed' as features of Computerised Accounting System.

key_points: Transparency and Control: Ensures transparent records with detailed audit trails. Restricts unauthorized access, maintaining high security and control over financial data.
Accuracy and Speed: Eliminates human mathematical errors. Processes vast amounts of accounting data instantaneously, generating real-time reports rapidly.

questions.solution: 'Transparency and Control' in a Computerised Accounting System (CAS) ensures that all financial transactions are cleanly recorded with precise audit trails. This establishes deep organizational transparency while giving management strict control through password-protected hierarchies that decisively prevent unauthorized access or illicit alterations. Concurrently, 'Accuracy and Speed' highlights the system's fundamental operational superiority. A CAS heavily relies on automated computations, which entirely eliminates human arithmetic errors, guaranteeing impeccable accuracy. Because processing power is utilized, it can ingest and calculate thousands of ledger entries almost instantly, generating complex financial statements at speeds unimaginable in manual accounting.
questions.solution_hindi: कम्प्यूटरीकृत लेखा प्रणाली (CAS) में 'पारदर्शिता और नियंत्रण' यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि सभी वित्तीय लेनदेन सटीक ऑडिट ट्रेल्स के साथ साफ-सुथरे ढंग से दर्ज किए गए हैं। यह संगठनात्मक पारदर्शिता स्थापित करता है जबकि प्रबंधन को पासवर्ड-संरक्षित पदानुक्रमों के माध्यम से सख्त नियंत्रण देता है जो अनधिकृत पहुंच या अवैध परिवर्तनों को रोकता है। साथ ही, 'शुद्धता और गति' प्रणाली की मौलिक परिचालन श्रेष्ठता को उजागर करती है। CAS स्वचालित गणनाओं पर बहुत अधिक निर्भर करता है, जो मानवीय गणितीय त्रुटियों को पूरी तरह से समाप्त कर देता है, त्रुटिहीन सटीकता की गारंटी देता है। क्योंकि प्रसंस्करण शक्ति का उपयोग किया जाता है, यह लगभग तुरंत हजारों खाता प्रविष्टियों की गणना कर सकता है, जिससे मैनुअल लेखांकन में अकल्पनीय गति से जटिल वित्तीय विवरण उत्पन्न होते हैं।

questions.text_english: Explain the two syntax forms of 'Lookup' function.

key_points: Vector form: Searches a one-row or one-column range (the lookup vector) for a value and returns a value from the same position in a second one-row or one-column range (the result vector).
Syntax: LOOKUP(lookup_value, lookup_vector, [result_vector]).
Array form: Searches the first row or column of a strict array for the specified value and returns a value from the same position in the last row or column of the array.
Syntax: LOOKUP(lookup_value, array).

The LOOKUP function in spreadsheet applications is rigorously designed to fetch specific data, utilizing two distinct syntax formats: the Vector form and the Array form. 

The Vector form is deployed when a user needs to search a specific single row or single column (known as the lookup_vector) to locate a desired value. Once the value is identified, it extracts the corresponding output from an identical position in a completely separate single row or column (the result_vector). Its strict syntax is: =LOOKUP(lookup_value, lookup_vector, [result_vector]). This grants heavy flexibility since the lookup and result columns don't have to be physically adjacent.

Conversely, the Array form is heavily utilized for more compact datasets. It blindly searches the very first row or column of a defined block of cells (the array) for the target value. Upon finding it, it automatically retrieves the corresponding value resting in the exact same position in the absolute last row or column of that identical array. Its simplified syntax is: =LOOKUP(lookup_value, array). This method demands that the target lookup values remain strictly sorted in ascending order to prevent severe retrieval errors.
questions.solution_hindi:
स्प्रेडशीट अनुप्रयोगों में LOOKUP फ़ंक्शन को विशिष्ट डेटा प्राप्त करने के लिए कठोरता से डिज़ाइन किया गया है, जिसमें दो अलग-अलग सिंटैक्स (वाक्य-विन्यास) प्रारूपों का उपयोग किया जाता है: वेक्टर रूप और सरणी (Array) रूप।

वेक्टर रूप (Vector form) का उपयोग तब किया जाता है जब उपयोगकर्ता को वांछित मूल्य का पता लगाने के लिए एक विशिष्ट एकल पंक्ति या एकल स्तंभ (जिसे lookup_vector के रूप में जाना जाता है) खोजने की आवश्यकता होती है। एक बार मूल्य की पहचान हो जाने पर, यह पूरी तरह से अलग एकल पंक्ति या स्तंभ (result_vector) में समान स्थिति से संबंधित आउटपुट निकालता है। इसका सिंटैक्स है: =LOOKUP(lookup_value, lookup_vector, [result_vector])।

इसके विपरीत, सरणी रूप (Array form) का उपयोग अधिक कॉम्पैक्ट डेटासेट के लिए किया जाता है। यह लक्ष्य मूल्य के लिए कोशिकाओं के एक परिभाषित ब्लॉक (सरणी) की पहली पंक्ति या स्तंभ को खोजता है। इसे खोजने पर, यह स्वचालित रूप से उस समान सरणी की अंतिम पंक्ति या स्तंभ में ठीक उसी स्थिति में स्थित संबंधित मूल्य को पुनः प्राप्त करता है। इसका सरलीकृत सिंटैक्स है: =LOOKUP(lookup_value, array)। इस पद्धति की मांग है कि गंभीर पुनर्प्राप्ति त्रुटियों को रोकने के लिए लक्ष्य लुकअप मानों को आरोही क्रम में कड़ाई से क्रमबद्ध किया जाए।
